capabilities: Edit JSON values and structure in a tree view
Edit JSON text in a CodeMirror source mode
Preserve comments and formatting in .jsonc files
Render JSON code blocks as collapsible trees
Validate JSON against a companion schema
disambiguation: Not a read-only JSON viewer; it edits .json and .jsonc files in place and only renders JSON code blocks in notes as read-only trees.
extras: Requires Obsidian 1.11.4+ (API keys stored in app.secretStorage). Claims the .json extension, so only one .json-handling plugin can be active; on conflict the file view is disabled but code-block rendering keeps working. Tree edits to .json re-serialize the whole document, which can reorder integer-like object keys; files with integers above 2^53 open read-only. Optional LLM repair sends the broken block to a user-configured endpoint (local server, Ollama, LM Studio, or Anthropic for Claude); secrets in the block are replaced with placeholders first. No telemetry or remote resources otherwise.
motivation: Built for personal use, released because it might be useful to others.
problem: Obsidian has no dedicated JSON editor, so .json files open as plain text and JSON snippets in notes stay unreadable, while ordinary re-serialization destroys comments and formatting.

relations.evidence: With the LLM Endpoint Manager plugin installed, the endpoint, its API key and the model come from there
Known examples: JSON Viewer (read-only viewer), JSON Collapsible, and Data Files Editor.
